arguments.name: term.cap
arguments.text: Capabilities used to decide which sequences are unhandled.

origin.details: Returns index, start, stop, error, translated, and esc for sequences the stated terminal would mishandle. The installed label for code 4 is non-SGR/hyperlink.
origin.value: A character vector, or a data frame for unhandled_ctl.
origin.example:
u <- unhandled_ctl(c("\033[41mhello world\033[m", "foo\033[22>m", "\033[999mbar", "baz \033[31#3m", "a\033[31k", "hello\033m world"), term.cap=c("bright", "256"))
cat(paste(u$index, u$start, u$stop, u$error, u$translated, encodeString(u$esc), sep=" "), sep="\n")
cat("\n")

arguments.name: term.cap
arguments.text: Capabilities used to decide which sequences are unhandled.

translation.details: Returns index, start, stop, error, translated, and esc for sequences the stated terminal would mishandle. The installed label for code 4 is non-SGR/hyperlink. A string is one element. None is a missing string. term_cap is the R term.cap argument.
translation.value: A list of strings, or a dict of columns for unhandled_ctl.
translation.example:
from fansi.unhandled_ctl import unhandled_ctl
rows = unhandled_ctl(["\033[41mhello world\033[m", "foo\033[22>m", "\033[999mbar", "baz \033[31#3m", "a\033[31k", "hello\033m world"], term_cap=["bright", "256"])
for i in range(len(rows["index"])):
    print(rows["index"][i], rows["start"][i], rows["stop"][i], rows["error"][i], rows["translated"][i], rows["esc"][i])
